author: Golden Gate Media
title: Police drone nabs suspected thief who pilfered California donut shop tip jar
text:
11 hours ago A small theft at a donut shop in Clovis, California triggered a swift and high-tech response from the Clovis Police Department, ending with an arrest and the return of stolen cash. Authorities say the incident unfolded on April 13, 2026, near the busy intersection of Fowler and Herndon, where officers were dispatched after a tips jar containing about $10 was taken from the counter.
Photo by Clovis Police “You better believe we protect some of the hardest aworkers in Clovis, our donut bakers!” the department said, underscoring the significance of the theft despite the small dollar amount. Police emphasized that “regardless what you think about tipping culture, a theft occurred,” and officers moved quickly to track down the suspect.
In a rapid escalation, the department’s Drone First Responder (DFR) program launched immediately, providing aerial surveillance before officers even reached the scene. From roughly 200 feet in the air, the drone located the suspect, guiding officers directly to the individual captured on camera moments earlier.
The suspect was arrested on suspicion of theft, and both the tips jar and the money were recovered and returned to the business. “Our Drone First Responder (DFR) launched immediately and was overhead just before officers arrived, leading officers to the suspect they had on camera from 200 feet in the air,” police said.
Officials credited the quick-thinking business staff for reporting the crime without delay and praised the coordinated effort among officers, dispatchers, and the drone pilot. The department added, “We thank the business for calling immediately, and we are thankful to our officers, dispatchers, and DFR pilot for the successful call for service.”
